summary: Today’s pulse tracks Anthony Fauci refuses to answer questions during US Senate hearing about Covid origins, Rescue teams face ‘race against time’ in search for trapped survivors as death toll in Japan rises to at least 13 – live updates, and Thousands in Spain return home but new heatwave raises wildfire fears. Across BBC, Guardian, and NPR, the strongest repeated signals are japan, earthquake, and fires. In the background, Oscar-winning songwriter Glen Hansard killed in crash and Spain faces ‘complex’ three days with risks of heatwave and strong winds reigniting some fires – Europe live keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Anthony Fauci refuses to answer questions during US Senate hearing about Covid origins
headlines.description: The former top US health official said he feared Republicans could try to trip him up and use his testimony to prosecute him for perjury.

headlines.title: Rescue teams face ‘race against time’ in search for trapped survivors as death toll in Japan rises to at least 13 – live updates
headlines.description: Emergency workers are continuing their search for survivors in southern Japan after yesterday’s powerful earthquake ‘Race against time’: Japan earthquake death toll rises as rescue teams search for missing An aerial view of a collapsed section of a bridge in the city of Yatsushiro after an earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 7.1 struck Japan’s southern Kumamoto prefecture: Japan’s Mainichi Shimbun newspaper has been speaking to people at the Nippon Paper Industries factory in Yatsushiro, where a chimney collapsed on to the site. “I never imagined something like this would happen,” said a 33-year-old man who worked at the factory. “I never thought that the chimney could collapse. I’m worried about the people inside.” He was off duty and at home when the earthquake struck, and was unharmed. The names of those rescued and those trapped have not yet been released. “Someone I know might be affected,” he said.

headlines.title: Thousands in Spain return home but new heatwave raises wildfire fears
headlines.description: Spain and France are both braced for the start of the fourth heatwave so far this summer and some fires have continued to burn.

headlines.title: Oscar-winning songwriter Glen Hansard killed in crash
headlines.description: Hansard, who was 56, won the best song Oscar for the 2007 low-budget musical film Once.

headlines.title: Spain faces ‘complex’ three days with risks of heatwave and strong winds reigniting some fires – Europe live
headlines.description: Authorities fear progress in containing the fires in the Gironde and Madrid regions may be set back by temperatures expected to hit the low 40s in Brussels The European Union’s crisis-management team is expecting difficult weeks ahead, fearing a further outbreak of wildfires in Italy and Greece as the summer goes on. “ A firefighter will focus on protecting people. They will focus on protecting houses, protecting a business, a company, because this is something that matters for all our society. And indeed, sometimes by focusing on that, they cannot extinguish fire, [as] they would do it if it would be just forest. So this is new, this is worrying. And of course also, this means that we need to adapt our methods of fighting the fires. ”

headlines.description: Chitral borders Afghanistan and isn't easy to reach. Breathtaking views abound in this remote mountainous region — as do rockslides and avalanches.

headlinePool.description: Medical adviser says he invokes right to refrain from answering questions, accusing Rand Paul of having ‘obvious obsession’ with him Fauci invokes fifth amendment and declines to testify But today’s hearing with Anthony Fauci was not an example of that, Peters said.

headlinePool.title: Next 12 hours ‘decisive’ for wildfire near Madrid, says Spanish PM
headlinePool.description: Comments by Pedro Sánchez come as extreme heat renews pressure on firefighters tackling blazes across southern Europe Europe live – latest updates The next 12 hours will be “decisive” for a large wildfire burning near Madrid, the Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has said, as extreme heat renews pressure on firefighters racing to control blazes across southern Europe. Temperatures pushed higher by climate breakdown are forecast to reach 39C on Wednesday in Bordeaux, where firefighters have kept a monster blaze in nearby pine forests from reaching the suburbs, and 37C in Madrid, west of which Spain’s largest wildfire on record is burning.

headlinePool.title: Burnham does not rule out tax rises for social care reform as he fast-tracks Louise Casey’s review – UK politics live
headlinePool.description: The prime minister says that current inefficiencies in the system will be tackled first, as he reveals final recommendations will be out by summer 2027 Andy Burnham is speaking now. In a reference to how he started campaing for social care reform almost two decades ago, he says it is good to see faces in the room “who’ve been on this journey with me for a long, a long time”. When someone in your family is receiving care, you look at everything through new eyes, don’t you? You notice things that maybe you didn’t notice before because you watch it so closely and so carefully. And I’ve just been really overwhelmed by their care, the skill in what they do, the professionalism. Can I just remind everybody that nobody thought we could get everybody in off the streets? So we can do difficult in this country and we can do it well.

headlinePool.title: Triple killer who dismembered bodies of two friends given whole-life jail sentence
headlinePool.description: James Desborough, who also strangled cellmate to death for snoring while awaiting trial, hid body fragments in Cornwall woods A triple killer who murdered and dismembered the bodies of two of his friends before strangling a third man to death in prison while awaiting trial has been told he will spent the rest of his life behind bars. Mr Justice Saini, who sentenced James Desborough, 40, at Winchester crown court, said the circumstances of the case were unique.

headlinePool.title: Flash floods and storms batter north-east US as deadly weather threatens millions
headlinePool.description: Lightning kills a New Jersey man as rescues, power outages and travel disruption hit region Bands of deadly, extreme weather including torrential rain and high winds sparked flash flooding and tornado warnings in several north eastern US states Tuesday night and into Wednesday, knocking out power for hundreds of thousands of people and playing havoc with travel. A 32-year-old man was killed on Tuesday afternoon in a lightning strike in Monroe township, New Jersey, authorities said.

headlinePool.title: Saudi Arabia joins US in strikes on Iran-backed militias in Iraq
headlinePool.description: US Central Command says proxy groups launched attacks against US bases and Saudi energy infrastructure.

headlinePool.title: Fauci invokes fifth amendment and declines to testify in Senate Covid hearing
headlinePool.description: Adviser to Trump and Biden for pandemic says Republican senator has ‘unhinged obsession’ with him US politics – live updates Anthony Fauci, who served as a key adviser to Donald Trump and Joe Biden during the Covid-19 pandemic, has refused to answer questions at a high-profile congressional hearing, accusing a Republican senator of having an “unhinged obsession” with him. Fauci, the veteran former director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (Niaid), invoked his constitutional right against incrimination when appearing before a Senate committee on Wednesday.

headlinePool.title: Four women accuse Jared Leto of criminal sexual conduct when they were teenagers
headlinePool.description: BBC documentary reports incidents alleged to have taken place when actor and musician was in 30s and 40s The actor and singer Jared Leto has been accused in a BBC documentary of criminal sexual conduct by four women, with the alleged offences taking place when the women were teenagers. The incidents reported by the BBC are alleged to have taken place between 2002 and 2016, when the actor was in his 30s and 40s. He is now 54.

headlinePool.title: Half of England officially in ‘exceptionally serious’ drought
headlinePool.description: Environment Agency names seven regions affected by unusually hot and dry weather and shortage of water Half of England is officially in drought, with July set to be the driest on record after winter floods, the Environment Agency has said. The “flash drought” developed quickly because of unusually low rainfall and high temperatures.
